function: Channel estimation: unsupervised denoising of the noisy uplink channel image, then inference of the full downlink channel from partial uplink observations in asymmetrical massive MIMO (pp. 1, 5-6).
system: TDD MIMO-OFDM, base station ULA with 128 transmit and 32 receive antennas, single-antenna users, 32 subcarriers, 28 GHz, 200 MHz; no RIS (p. 9, Table I).
method: Residual CNNs: unsupervised Denoising-Net with masked centre pixel, then supervised AsNet with adaptive attention modules; offline training with Adam and MSE loss (pp. 5-7).
data_channel: Public DeepMIMO O1 ray-tracing scenario at 28 GHz, users at 1.5 m; noisy uplink image as input, downlink channel as label; same dataset for training and testing (pp. 8-9).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on a 4:1 split of the same O1-28 data; tests sweep SNR, Nr/Nt ratio, and uniform or random receive-antenna selection (pp. 8-11).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, LMMSE, OMP with K-SVD. Learned: ChannelNet [27], Bayesian neural network (BNN); traditional 3x3 residual network for the denoiser (p. 9).
metrics: NMSE of the downlink channel inference; mean SNR after denoising (denoising gain); validation loss in the neuron-design ablations (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Analytical FLOPs order of AsNet, O(23NdNcNtK + 15NdNaNtK + 27NdNaNbNtK); no measured runtime or parameter count (p. 8).
openness: none: no code or data link; trains on the public DeepMIMO dataset [33] (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 8: "public DeepMIMO ray-tracing dataset" (the O1 scenario, 28 GHz, Table I on p. 9) is the data used to train and test.
q2_support: p. 8: "split as 4:1" train and test of the same O1-28 data; not met because the Nr sweep of p. 11 never states that a model trained at one Nr is reused at another, and no new scenario, band or dataset is tested (p. 13 leaves real-world data for future work).
q3_support: p. 9: "ChannelNet algorithm proposed in [27]" and "Bayesian Neural Networks (BNN) [48]" are the learned baselines, with "LS and LMMSE" and OMP with K-SVD as non-learned ones, all compared on NMSE (Fig. 8, p. 10).
q4_support: p. 8: "floating point operations (FLOPs) as the metric", with the order of the FLOPs of FDAM, AAM and AsNet given in Section IV-D.
q5_support: p. 8: "public DeepMIMO ray-tracing dataset" is used for training and testing; the paper gives no link to its own code.
notes: The first page of the PDF holds the title Knowledge-Driven Channel Estimation for Asymmetrical Massive MIMO Systems and DOI 10.1109/TVT.2024.3456102. Area 2 because the learned method estimates the downlink channel (denoising plus uplink-to-downlink inference) and NMSE is the main metric. q2 is 0 by the explicit-statement rule: the Nr sweep on p. 11 could be read as a test with another number of antennas, so the reviewer may confirm. q5 rests on the public DeepMIMO dataset only.
